case_title: VIPIN JAISWAL v. STATE OF A.P.
high_court_outcome: Acquitted two relatives, maintained conviction of appellant
neutral_facts: The accused, the husband of the deceased, was charged with causing the death of his wife, who died from burn injuries. The prosecution alleged that the deceased was subjected to physical and mental torture by her husband and in-laws for not providing sufficient dowry. The accused claimed that his wife had left behind a suicide note stating that she committed suicide due to harassment by her parents, not by her husband or in-laws. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 304 and 498A of the IPC, citing harassment and cruelty. The High Court acquitted two other relatives but upheld the conviction of the accused. The Supreme Court reviewed the case, noting that the demand for Rs.50,000/- by the accused for a computer was not a dowry demand as it was not connected to the marriage. The court also found that the suicide note, written by the deceased, cast doubt on the prosecution's claim of harassment and cruelty. The court ultimately acquitted the accused, stating that the prosecution failed to prove the essential ingredients of the offenses beyond reasonable doubt.
